final_qi.question: Is Abruzzo-Erikson syndrome linked to the CHD7 mutation?
final_qi.long_answer: Abruzzo-Erikson syndrome is an earlier eponym for the condition that is now grouped under CHARGE syndrome (characterised by Coloboma, Heart defects, Choanal atresia, Retarded growth/development, Genital anomalies and Ear anomalies). The great majority of individuals diagnosed with CHARGE/Abruzzo-Erikson syndrome carry heterozygous pathogenic variants in the CHD7 gene. Therefore, the syndrome is indeed linked to CHD7 mutation.

Very few people with CHARGE will have 100% of its known features. Section: Introduction
Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is a disorder in which the spine starts abnormally curving sideways (scoliosis) between the ages of 10 and 18 years old.[1][2][3] Generally, AIS occurs during the growth spurt associated with adolescence.[4][5][6] In some teens, the curvature is progressive, meaning that it gets worse over time,[7] however, AIS more commonly manifests only as a mild curvature.

final_answer.long_answer: Abruzzo-Erikson syndrome is an earlier eponym for the condition that is now grouped under CHARGE syndrome (characterised by Coloboma, Heart defects, Choanal atresia, Retarded growth/development, Genital anomalies and Ear anomalies). The great majority of individuals diagnosed with CHARGE/Abruzzo-Erikson syndrome carry heterozygous pathogenic variants in the CHD7 gene. Therefore, the syndrome is indeed linked to CHD7 mutation.
